patch_description:
Reverts to the empirically strongest known structure (2 distinct circuit
parameters: a global RY angle and a global RZ angle that is reused as the
controlled-RZ angle across three entangling shells — nearest-neighbor,
skip-2, and antipodal), which previously scored 0.61, clearly outperforming
the 4-parameter even/odd split variant that collapsed training (score 0.40).
The even/odd split broke the ring's rotational symmetry and evidently created
a harder optimization landscape (the model never reached the convergence
threshold and stayed near chance accuracy), so it is dropped entirely rather
than patched.

On top of the proven 2-parameter backbone, a final global RY(theta_ry) mixer
layer is appended after the three entangling shells, reusing the *existing*
theta_ry parameter (no new distinct parameter name is introduced, so the
circuit-parameter count stays at 2, i.e. n_params=4 total with gain/bias).
This mirrors the "output mixer" idea from the very first seed (which used a
dedicated theta_ry_out and scored 0.59) but without paying the parameter-count
penalt: since parameter economy is stated to dominate the score at every
count, sharing the mixer angle with the input rotation instead of introducing
a fresh one is the way to capture a similar effect for free. The extra RY
layer gives the optimizer one more place (still governed by the same 1
learned scalar) to re-align qubit Bloch vectors with the fixed two-qubit
readout observable right before measurement, which should help push the
worst-group margin up slightly without touching the train/test generalization
gap or the parameter count that the evolutionary score rewards most heavily.

All shells keep the full rotational/reflection symmetry of the qubit ring
(no even/odd anisotropy), which — combined with the "no full K8 graph"
lesson already encoded in the base design (distance-3 edges are deliberately
omitted, since a prior experiment showed the fully-connected 28-edge graph
dilutes the per-edge rotation and hurts accuracy) — keeps the circuit in the
regime that is known to train reliably to 100% training accuracy while
generalizing best among all tested variants so far.
